hero.title: Electromagnetic Induction — How Every Generator & Motor Works
hero.hook: Every time you charge your phone, switch on a fan, or use a transformer, electromagnetic induction is doing the work. Faraday discovered it in 1831 by moving a magnet through a coil. That one experiment powers the entire modern world — and it's worth 5 marks in your boards.

hook_section.scenario: Move a bar magnet into a coil of wire — a current appears in the coil even though there's no battery. Pull the magnet out — current flows in the opposite direction. Hold the magnet still — current drops to zero. The current exists only when something changes. What is changing? The magnetic flux through the coil.
hook_section.bridge: This is the principle behind generators (mechanical energy → electricity), transformers (changing voltage), and induction cooktops. Faraday's Law and Lenz's Law together explain both the magnitude and direction of the induced EMF.
hook_section.punchline: EMF is induced when magnetic flux changes. The induced current always opposes the change that caused it.

concept_section.analogy: Imagine a lazy river (the coil). Normally it flows steadily. Push a dam in (changing flux) — water rushes to resist the dam. Pull the dam out — water rushes back. The river always reacts against what you do to it. That's Lenz's Law — induced current opposes the change in flux, like a stubborn river.
concept_section.principle: Faraday's Law: EMF = −N × ΔΦ/Δt (N = number of turns, Φ = magnetic flux = B·A·cosθ). Lenz's Law: induced current direction is such that it opposes the change in flux (negative sign in Faraday's Law).
concept_section.reveal_prompt: Tap each concept to explore it 👇

reveals.question: 🌀 How to increase induced EMF?
reveals.answer: Increase N (more turns), increase rate of flux change (move magnet faster), use stronger magnet, increase coil area. EMF ∝ N × ΔΦ/Δt.

reveals.question: 🔄 Lenz's Law in practice?
reveals.answer: Magnet's N pole entering coil → coil develops N pole facing the magnet (to repel it, opposing entry). Same pole, opposing the motion. This conserves energy — you must do work against this opposition.

reveals.question: ⚡ What is motional EMF?
reveals.answer: A conductor of length l moving with velocity v in magnetic field B develops EMF = Bvl (perpendicular motion). This is how generators work — rotating coils in a magnetic field.

reveals.question: 🔁 AC vs DC generator?
reveals.answer: AC generator: slip rings → alternating current output. DC generator: commutator → unidirectional (pulsating DC) output. Both use coil rotation in magnetic field.

points: Magnetic flux: Φ = B·A·cosθ; maximum when B ⊥ plane of coil (θ=0°), zero when B ∥ plane
Faraday's Law: EMF = −NΔΦ/Δt; magnitude proportional to rate of flux change
Lenz's Law: induced current opposes the change — consequence of energy conservation
Motional EMF: EMF = Bvl for a conductor moving perpendicular to field
Eddy currents: induced in bulk conductors; cause heating (used in induction cooktops, brakes)

exam_questions.question: State Faraday's laws of electromagnetic induction. A coil of 200 turns, area 0.05m² is in a field that changes from 0.1T to 0.5T in 0.02s. Find induced EMF.
State Lenz's Law. How does it relate to conservation of energy?
What is the SI unit of magnetic flux?

quiz.q: A coil of 100 turns has flux changing from 0.02 Wb to 0.06 Wb in 0.4s. Induced EMF is:
Lenz's Law is a consequence of:
quiz.exp: Lenz's Law states induced current opposes change in flux. If it aided the change, energy would be created from nothing — violating conservation of energy.

quiz.q: A straight conductor of length 0.5m moves at 2m/s perpendicular to a 0.4T field. Induced EMF is:
Eddy currents are used beneficially in:
quiz.exp: Induction furnaces use eddy currents to heat metals without direct contact. The changing magnetic field induces large eddy currents in the metal, generating heat.

flipcards.front: State Faraday's First Law of EMI
flipcards.back: Whenever the magnetic flux linked with a circuit changes, an EMF is induced in the circuit
Induced current direction opposes the change in magnetic flux that caused it
EMF = Bvl (B = field, v = velocity, l = conductor length, all mutually perpendicular)

flipcards.front: Difference: AC generator vs DC generator?
flipcards.back: AC: slip rings → alternating output. DC: commutator → unidirectional output.
Circulating currents induced in bulk conductors by changing magnetic flux; cause heating
